claude_take: What strikes me about today's set is how much energy goes into renaming things instead of fixing them. The White House didn't regulate AI, it rebranded it as "super intelligence" and collected a voluntary, unenforceable pledge from the same companies whose own safety staff are resigning and calling the culture broken from the inside. Paramount and Warner Bros. did a smaller version of the same move, settling on a new combined name, Skydance, while the executives who ran the old film business quietly get swept out. The one place real guardrails actually showed up today was the least glamorous: Apple's visual effects crew, who won enforceable AI protections not through a pledge but through a union contract, line by line.
claude_take_title: They Rebranded It Instead of Regulating It

items.headline: OpenAI Safety Employee Resigns, Says Company's Culture Is 'Broken'
items.summary: An OpenAI employee resigned this week and publicly accused the company of letting safety culture erode as it races to ship products faster. The departure extends a string of safety-team exits at OpenAI over the past two years and renews scrutiny of how frontier labs balance commercial pressure against risk review. It lands just as regulators have opened a broader probe into how AI companies police themselves.

items.headline: Trump Rebrands AI as 'Super Intelligence,' Tech CEOs Sign Voluntary Safety Pledge
items.summary: President Trump signed an executive order directing the federal government to refer to AI as "super intelligence," and hosted the heads of Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, Nvidia and xAI as they signed a one-page White House Accord pledging layered internal and external safety audits. Trump called the pact "morally binding," though it carries no legal force and leaves enforcement entirely to the companies themselves. The move caps a broader push by the administration to frame AI dominance as central to its agenda while resisting binding regulation.

items.headline: Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Will Create Skydance Corp
items.summary: David Ellison confirmed that the combined company emerging from Paramount Skydance's roughly $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery will be named Skydance Corp, with the deal expected to close within days. Both HBO Max and Paramount+ will continue as separate streaming brands rather than being merged into one. The name reveal caps a turbulent run-up marked by antitrust delays and leadership uncertainty atop Warner's film division.

items.headline: Apple Studios Visual Effects Workers Ratify Their First IATSE Contract
items.summary: In-house visual effects artists at Apple Studios have ratified their first union contract with IATSE, securing minimum-hour guarantees, overtime protections and new artificial-intelligence safeguards drawn from the broader IATSE-AMPTP agreement. The deal extends a wave of VFX unionization that has already reached Marvel, Disney and the Avatar franchise. It signals that enforceable AI-use protections are becoming a standard feature of visual effects labor contracts across the industry.

items.headline: Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Bombs at the Box Office Despite Hefty Budget
items.summary: "Digger," Alejandro G. Iñárritu's eco-thriller starring Tom Cruise as an oil tycoon, opened far below expectations on a production budget that reportedly swelled past $160 million, landing a 41% Rotten Tomatoes score and one of Cruise's weakest wide openings in years. It lost the weekend to Amazon MGM's "Verity," an adaptation of Colleen Hoover's novel starring Anne Hathaway. The underperformance renews questions about whether star power and scale alone can still carry a big-budget, director-driven film outside an established franchise.

items.headline: French Unions Escalate Strikes as Lecornu Faces Oct. 7 Budget Deadline
items.summary: French unions staged a fresh round of strikes and protests this week to pressure Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu over his predecessor's austerity budget, deepening the unrest that erupted when the plan was first unveiled. Lecornu must send a full draft of the 2026 budget to a parliament split into three hostile blocs by October 7, with the hard left threatening an immediate no-confidence motion. The standoff underscores how fragile his government remains as it tries to narrow France's deficit without triggering its own collapse.

items.headline: CFDA Names Hildy Kuryk Interim CEO After Steven Kolb's Exit
items.summary: The Council of Fashion Designers of America named Hildy Kuryk, a former Vogue communications executive, as interim CEO after Steven Kolb resigned following video that showed him physically restraining PETA protesters who stormed a runway show. Kuryk, who is not a candidate for the permanent role, will lead the organization while a search firm runs a three-to-six-month hunt for Kolb's successor. The episode has put a spotlight on how fashion institutions handle animal-rights protests during an already tense show season.

items.headline: Arendt's Banality of Evil
items.headline_fr: La banalité du mal selon Hannah Arendt
items.summary: Coined by Hannah Arendt after she observed the 1961 trial of Nazi official Adolf Eichmann, "the banality of evil" describes how history's worst atrocities are often carried out not by fanatics but by ordinary bureaucrats who stop thinking critically about their actions and simply follow orders within a system. Arendt argued that this thoughtlessness, rather than deep-seated hatred, is what allows ordinary people to become complicit in atrocity. The idea remains a touchstone for understanding how institutions, corporations and bureaucracies can produce harm through conformity and unreflective obedience rather than malice.
items.summary_fr: Forgée par Hannah Arendt après avoir observé le procès du responsable nazi Adolf Eichmann en 1961, la notion de « banalité du mal » décrit comment les pires atrocités de l'histoire sont souvent commises non par des fanatiques, mais par de simples bureaucrates qui cessent de réfléchir à leurs actes et se contentent d'obéir aux ordres au sein d'un système. Arendt soutenait que c'est cette absence de pensée critique, plus que la haine, qui permet à des gens ordinaires de devenir complices de l'atrocité. Cette idée reste une référence essentielle pour comprendre comment les institutions, les entreprises et les administrations peuvent engendrer le mal par conformisme et obéissance irréfléchie plutôt que par méchanceté.
